issue.title: BeadUpdateFieldsWire.resolution cannot express clearing a resolution over the wire
issue.description:
Found 2026-08-16 during the audit that accompanied the bead-event resolution round-trip fix (sase-core 2233171); filed as follow-up rather than folded into that tale.

crates/sase_core/src/bead/mutation.rs:100-105 in the sibling sase-core repo declares:

  pub resolution: Option<Option<BeadResolutionWire>>,

as a plain derived double option. Serde's derived deserializer maps JSON null onto the OUTER None, not Some(None), so a caller sending {"resolution": null} to mean 'clear the resolution' is silently read as 'leave unchanged'. There is no way to express a clear over this wire, and the misread is silent -- no error, the field just does not change.

This is the same asymmetric-double-option bug class already fixed on the event wire: bead/events.rs's issue_updated resolution field had it, and it produced a non-round-trip-stable event that wedged the whole bead store for hours. The fix there was to pair the field with the presence-preserving deserializer now shared at crates/sase_core/src/serde_option.rs (deserialize_present_option).

Difference in severity: the events.rs field also carried skip_serializing_if, which is what made it non-round-trip-stable and therefore store-wedging. mutation.rs's field has no skip_serializing_if, so it cannot wedge anything -- it can only silently drop a clear request. The audit found no live caller that depends on clearing through this wire, which is why it was filed instead of changed.

Scope: decide whether clearing should be expressible here. If yes, apply deserialize_present_option and add a round-trip test alongside the ones added for events.rs. If no, make the impossibility explicit -- change the type so the unusable state cannot be constructed, or reject an explicit null -- so the next reader does not assume a clear will work. Cross-repo: ../sase-core.

payload.entry: RELATED: sase-mr — the other sase-core follow-up from the same incident; both are in the bead event/mutation wire layer.
